Formula to use to match TradingView (one change: round the half-length, do not floor it)
function hma(closes, n = 9) {              // closes: full history, oldest → newest; returns the latest value
  const half = Math.round(n / 2);          // ← TradingView/Fyers: round(9/2) = 5   (Nubra today: floor → 4)
  const root = Math.round(Math.sqrt(n));   // 3 for n = 9 (floor/round/ceil all give 3 here)
  const wma = (a, len) => a.map((_, i) => i < len - 1 ? null :
      a.slice(i - len + 1, i + 1).reduce((s, v, k) => s + (k + 1) * v, 0) / (len * (len + 1) / 2));
  const diff = wma(closes, half).map((v, i) => { const w = wma(closes, n)[i]; return v == null || w == null ? null : 2 * v - w; });
  const out = wma(diff.map(v => v ?? NaN), root);
  return out[out.length - 1];
}
Verified by recomputing from the identical candles; the round-half-up choice is what Fyers (TradingView library) shows. TradingView's reference page was not readable here.

109.cause: The five Ichimoku lines are the same on both charts, but the legends read them differently: Nubra lists them in a different order and shows the spans and lagging line un-displaced, while TradingView shows the displaced value at the crosshair. Matching column pairs (conversion, base) are equal on 144 of 144 days at the same bar; the spans and lagging line are equal on 144 of 144 days once shifted by the 26-bar displacement and re-ordered.
109.summary: Same five lines; Nubra's legend shows the displaced cloud lines un-displaced and in a different order (verified numerically with a 26-bar shift, 144 of 144 days). How the cloud is drawn on the chart was not compared visually.

101.cause: Nubra's first line reproduces the standard Chande-Kroll formula (ATR with RMA smoothing, high/low) on 115 of 144 days (the other days differ slightly, likely ATR warm-up) and its second line equals Fyers on every day. Fyers' first line (stop long) is different from Nubra's by up to about 5,000 points, and no window variant I tried (low window 8 to 12, stop window 7 to 11) reproduces it. Cause not found; needs a closer look, possibly Fyers' own variant.

087.cause: Nubra and Fyers differ by about 1.5% (Nubra/Fyers ratio 1.02 early, 0.985 late) and the gap does not shrink over time (average 0.10, 0.11, 0.09, 0.09 across the four quarters), so it is not warm-up. TradingView's formula (10000 x change of EMA³ of ln close) reproduces Fyers on only 32 of 91 days and no candidate reproduces Nubra, so the cause is not found; the likely suspects are the EMA seeding and whether the log is applied.

128.cause: Same formula, different scale: Nubra shows Bollinger Bandwidth as a percentage (9.44) where TradingView shows the ratio (0.094, displayed as 0.09). Nubra divided by 100 equals Fyers on 144 of 144 days (within Fyers' 2-decimal display).

152.cause: Different definitions under the same name. Fyers (TradingView) Median Price is (high + low) / 2, reproduced on 144 of 144 days. Nubra's "Median" has a Length input (default 3) and equals the 3-bar average of (high + low) / 2 on 144 of 144 days. At the same candle the two numbers differ by hundreds of points.
152.summary: Different definition: TradingView = (high+low)/2 of the bar; Nubra = 3-bar average of (high+low)/2. Each reproduces its own numbers on 144 of 144 days.

150.cause: The middle line is the same on both charts: Nubra's first line equals Fyers' second line on 108 of 144 days, and on the other 36 it differs by at most 0.40 points (0.0003%, EMA warm-up). The bands differ because the defaults and definition differ: Nubra uses multiplier 2 with a separate ATR length of 10, Fyers uses multiplier 1 with the true range over the same 20 bars (this looks like the older TradingView "KC" study). Per the reviewer's rule the reference defaults are the correct ones; to compare the band maths itself Nubra would have to be set to multiplier 1 and the true-range option, which it does not offer.
150.summary: Middle line equal (max gap 0.40 points); bands differ because defaults/definition differ (Nubra: multiplier 2, ATR length 10; reference: multiplier 1, true range over the same length).

194.cause: The three central values (pivot, bottom and top of the range) are the same set on both charts on 144 of 144 days; their order differs from day to day. Fyers' CPR indicator also plots 13 more pivot levels (support and resistance); Nubra's legend shows "—" for them, so they are either off by default or not drawn. This is a feature difference, not a value difference.
194.summary: Central values equal as a set on 144 of 144 days (order varies); Fyers additionally plots 13 pivot levels that Nubra shows as "—".

102.cause: Not comparable line by line: Nubra shows one stop at a time (the other side prints "—") and takes two inputs (ATR period 22, multiplier 3), while Fyers shows both stops and has three inputs (length 22, ATR length 22, multiplier 3). Needs a direction-aware comparison.

059.cause: Same name, different indicator: Fyers' "RSI Momentum Divergence" is a fast RSI minus a slow RSI (inputs 5 and 14), Nubra's has five inputs (RSI length 14, pivot settings, 60) and a divergence-detection design. The numbers (45.7 vs 13.2) are not comparable.

096.cause: The parameter sets differ: Nubra has ATR period and multiplier (defaults 20 and 2) while Fyers has three inputs (5, 10, 2.5).
